Releases are cut by pushing a git tag, and CI does the rest. This comes from a stored project convention, not something I could confirm in the repo.

1. Make sure `main` has the commits you want to ship.
2. Pick the next version, which has the form `vYYYY.MM.N`. `N` is the release counter within that month. For example, the memory's example is `v2026.09.2`. Today is 2026-10-02, so the first October release would be `v2026.10.1`. Check `git tag --list 'v2026.10.*'` first to see whether that number is taken.
3. Create the tag and push it, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
4. CI builds and publishes. Never publish by hand.

I found no CI config or release scripts in the repo, so I can't tell you which workflow the tag triggers or what checks run first. I also haven't checked whether `N` resets each month or whether tags need to be annotated or signed. I haven't run any git commands, so no tag has been created or pushed. Let me know if you want me to check existing tags and propose the next version.
